descriptors.evidence: Exactly 2 distinct values ('no','yes'), mean_value_length 2.76, uniqueness_ratio 0.0001 across 25258 occurrences — a clean binary flag. Several other fields (feature_3, feature_7, feature_12, feature_15, feature_17, feature_31) share this identical yes/no shape, so which specific product attribute this flag represents cannot be distinguished from values alone.

1613 distinct values over 8145 occurrences (uniqueness_ratio 0.198) with finish/material-style samples ('acacia','acorn','acrylic','aged brass') strongly suggest a Color/Finish attribute, the classic high-cardinality variant-defining field in furniture. feature_11 shares near-identical vocabulary and cardinality shape, so which is the primary color field vs. a secondary finish field is unresolved.

Lexically-first samples are wildly heterogeneous: an empty string, the bare digit '0', a color-count breakdown ('2 taupe , 2 teal , 2 white'), a lone punctuation value (';'), and a templated bracket placeholder ('[ tied to : color ]'), across 4686 distinct values / 26295 occurrences. This mix of numeric noise, punctuation-only entries and placeholder text suggests a poorly-normalized/derived column rather than one coherent attribute.

2 distinct ('no','yes'), uniqueness_ratio 0.0001, 30534 occurrences — the highest-volume boolean flag in the set, implying a near-universally-populated attribute, but nothing in the values identifies which one.

distinct_values (71) exactly equals occurrences (71), uniqueness_ratio 1.0 — every populated row is unique. Samples ('120767wht','1wf54a0jsv','140-c6501s-t') are short alphanumeric codes typical of a manufacturer part/model number; numeric_parseable_fraction is only 0.0282, confirming mostly non-pure-numeric codes.

Only 161 occurrences (sparse) with 78 distinct values (uniqueness_ratio 0.4845) but numeric_parseable_fraction of only 0.1304 — meaning most of the 78 distinct values are NOT numeric even though the lexically-first samples ('1','2','330','1795','140780') look numeric (digit strings sort before letter strings, so a numeric minority dominates the alphabetically-first sample). Reads as a sparse secondary code/model-number field, but the internal inconsistency leaves real doubt.

71 distinct values, all lowercase country names in alphabetical order (afghanistan, argentina, australia, bahrain, bangladesh), 34034 occurrences, extremely low uniqueness_ratio (0.0021) — a textbook Country-of-Origin field.

2 distinct ('no','yes'), uniqueness_ratio 0.0002, 8696 occurrences — a lower-volume boolean flag than feature_0/feature_3, suggesting it applies to a narrower product subset, but the specific attribute is unidentifiable from values.

16 distinct decor-style values (boho, coastal, country, 'country / farmhouse') over 18227 occurrences with very low uniqueness (0.0009) — canonical home-decor Style attribute, one of the most common shopper search facets.

Only 9 distinct 'X wood' tone values (dark brown wood, espresso wood, gray wood, light wood), including a manual-entry typo ('esptresso wood') confirming hand-curated categorical data — a coarse wood-tone/finish color field, likely variant-defining.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9991 (essentially all values numeric) with short mean_value_length (2.03), implying small integers — consistent with a count field (drawers, shelves, pieces, or reviews), but nothing distinguishes which count.

1294 distinct values / 7719 occurrences (uniqueness 0.1676) with vocabulary near-identical to feature_1 ('acrylic','aged brass') — almost certainly another Color/Finish-type field, but cannot be distinguished from feature_1 by values alone; flagged as a genuine field-identity ambiguity.

3 distinct values ('','no','yes') over 7541 occurrences — a yes/no flag with an explicit missing-value token, otherwise identical in shape to feature_0/feature_3/feature_7; specific meaning unidentifiable.

77 distinct material names ('acacia wood','acrylic','aluminium','aluminum'), including both British and American spellings of aluminum — a classic Material attribute, coarser-grained than the finish-name fields feature_1/feature_11.

12 distinct values dominated by 'full'/'full warranty'/'limited' — reads as a Warranty-Type classification (full vs. limited), distinct from the duration-oriented feature_26 and the verbose feature_34, though overlap among the three warranty-shaped fields is real.
3 distinct values ('','no','yes') over 12555 occurrences — same yes/no-with-missing shape as feature_12/feature_17; specific real-world meaning cannot be inferred from values.
10 distinct values ('full','full assembly','full assembly needed','light') plainly describe Assembly Required level — a well-known, heavily-filtered furniture facet.
3 distinct values ('','no','yes') over 7459 occurrences — indistinguishable in shape from feature_12/feature_15; cannot identify the specific attribute from values alone.

numeric_parseable_fraction 1.0 (fully numeric) with short values (mean_value_length 2.98) — a small-scale physical measurement (e.g. leg diameter or material thickness in inches). Sample values are the lexically-first distinct strings, not necessarily the smallest magnitudes, so the true value range/unit cannot be confirmed.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9999, mean_value_length 2.89, 37136 occurrences — a clean numeric measurement field of unknown unit; shares the same decimal-string shape as feature_18/feature_20/feature_21/feature_35, making the specific physical quantity indistinguishable.

57110 occurrences — the single most-populated field in the whole set — with numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9996, suggesting a near-universal core spec (weight, price, or a primary dimension) that shoppers commonly range-filter on, but which spec it is cannot be pinned down from values alone.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9993 over 46687 occurrences, same decimal-string profile as feature_18/feature_19/feature_20/feature_35 — an indistinguishable member of what looks like a family of dimension/weight-type numeric columns.

93 distinct art/pattern-style values ('abstract','abstract cubism','abstract/geometric') plus a bracketed placeholder ('[ doesnotapply ]') mirroring the templated-noise style seen in feature_2 — likely an Art Subject/Pattern-Theme attribute for wall-decor items, overlapping in vocabulary with feature_28.

Itemized samples ('( 1 ) stand mixer , ( 1 ) 6 quart bowl , ...') describing box contents across varied product types (bed frame, kitchen cart, shower curtain liner) — a 'What's Included' / package-contents free-text field; 2706 distinct values over only 6881 occurrences (uniqueness 0.3933) confirms high per-product variability.

250 distinct 'NN % material' values ('100 % cotton','100 % fine porcelain') but low uniqueness_ratio (0.023) over 10860 occurrences — values repeat heavily, so despite free-text formatting this behaves as a bounded Material-Composition enum.

Long prose instructions ('brush off dust then wipe clean with a damp cloth...') with the highest mean_value_length in the set (50.76) and high uniqueness (0.2215 over 15802 occurrences, 3500 distinct) — a Care/Cleaning-Instructions text field.

Only 7 distinct values ('1 year','90 days','lifetime') over 29209 occurrences (uniqueness 0.0002) — a canonical Warranty-Duration field. One outlier value embeds a full sentence and a support URL, a data-quality anomaly rather than the field's true shape.

uniqueness_ratio 0.9785 (2004 distinct / 2048 occurrences) with barcode-like values ('069556530416' — 12 digits, UPC-A shaped) and structured codes ('06.mmfpbdv.44') — a UPC/model-number identifier. One sample ('# ref !') looks like a leaked spreadsheet #REF! error, signalling real data-quality contamination in this column.

99 distinct decorative pattern/shape values ('abstract/novelty','amphora','arabesque') over 9122 occurrences — a Pattern/Shape-type attribute, but its vocabulary overlaps with feature_22 ('abstract') closely enough that which product facet (rug pattern vs. vessel shape vs. print theme) it represents is genuinely unclear.

70 distinct style/theme values ('american traditional','antik','apothecary','asian inspired') over 19221 occurrences — a Style/Theme attribute, likely finer-grained or category-specific compared to feature_8's broader decor-style vocabulary (boho/coastal/farmhouse); plausibly related but not confidently the same field.

Only 546 occurrences with 493 distinct values (uniqueness 0.9029) and long descriptive samples ('1881 oahu hawaii vintage map','a pelican and other birds near a pool the floating feather 1680') including dimensions embedded in text ('40 x 64') — an Artwork/Print Title field for wall-art SKUs, sparsely populated because it only applies to a subset of the catalog.
2 distinct values ('no','yes'), uniqueness_ratio 0.0002, 10779 occurrences — same clean binary shape as feature_0/feature_3/feature_7; specific meaning unidentifiable from values alone.

2176 distinct values / 7306 occurrences (uniqueness 0.2978) dominated by descriptive '2-tone X' color names ('2 tone espresso','2-tone brown','2-tone latte') — a Color/Finish field, but one sample ('0354-92 ; 0354-92') is a raw internal code rather than a color name, showing the column mixes human-readable colors with SKU-like codes; also overlaps vocabulary-wise with feature_1/feature_11.

113 distinct compound material-composition strings ('10 % mdf/ 10 % half pu/ ... / 60 % metal frame','100 % cotton') with low uniqueness_ratio (0.0156) over 7247 occurrences — values repeat, so despite compound formatting this behaves as a bounded Material-Composition attribute akin to feature_24 but with multi-material breakdowns.

112 distinct, often verbose warranty-style phrases ('1 year from the date of purchase.','1 year limited manufacturer warranty') over 21320 occurrences — reads as a longer-form Warranty Description alongside the terser feature_26 and the type-oriented feature_14; the three-way split among warranty-shaped fields cannot be fully resolved from values.

numeric_parseable_fraction 0.9997 over 15125 occurrences, same short-decimal-string profile as feature_18/feature_19/feature_20/feature_21 — another undifferentiated member of the apparent dimension/weight numeric-field family.
